mcqs.question: Which property would be most suitable for classifying a collection of objects into the groups “magnetic” and “non‑magnetic”?
mcqs.explanation: Magnetism directly tells whether an object is attracted to a magnet, which is the defining feature of the two groups. Color, size, and weight do not determine magnetic behavior, so they would not give a correct classification.

mcqs.question: If you group classroom items based only on whether they are solid or liquid, how many groups will you obtain?
mcqs.explanation: Using a single property – the state of matter – divides the items into two distinct categories: solids and liquids. Hence exactly two groups are formed.

mcqs.learning_point: Creating groups using more than one property
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes grouping objects using more than one property?

options.A: Using only one property at a time
options.B: Combining two or more properties to form sub‑groups
options.D: Grouping objects without considering any property

mcqs.answer: Combining two or more properties to form sub‑groups
mcqs.explanation: When more than one property is used, each object is examined for each selected property, and objects that share the same combination of properties are placed together, creating finer sub‑groups. The other options describe incorrect or random methods.

mcqs.learning_point: Explaining why a material belongs to a group
mcqs.question: Why is wood placed in the group “non‑conductors of heat”?

options.A: Because it melts at a low temperature
options.B: Because it allows heat to pass quickly
options.C: Because it does not allow heat to pass easily

mcqs.answer: Because it does not allow heat to pass easily
mcqs.explanation: Wood has low thermal conductivity, meaning heat moves through it slowly. Therefore it is classified as a non‑conductor of heat. Melting point, rapid heat transfer, and metallic nature are unrelated to this classification.

mcqs.learning_point: Using classification to identify suitable materials
mcqs.question: Which material would be most suitable for making a cooking pot, based on the classification of heat‑conducting properties?
mcqs.explanation: Iron is a good conductor of heat, allowing the pot to heat evenly and quickly. Plastic, glass, and wood are poor conductors and would either melt, crack, or not transfer heat efficiently.

mcqs.question: A student wants to sort a mixed collection of objects (coins, paper clips, rubber bands) to find which are magnetic. Which property should she use for the classification?
mcqs.explanation: The goal is to separate magnetic from non‑magnetic items, so the relevant property is magnetism. Color, size, and texture do not indicate magnetic behavior.

mcqs.question: Which of the following shows a correct way to group objects using only one property?

options.A: Grouping all red items together regardless of material
options.B: Grouping items as “metal” and “non‑metal” based on magnetism
options.C: Grouping by both color and weight at the same time
options.D: Grouping objects randomly without any property

mcqs.answer: Grouping items as “metal” and “non‑metal” based on magnetism
mcqs.explanation: Option B uses a single, clear property—magnetism—to separate metals (which are magnetic) from non‑metals. Option A relies only on color, which does not reflect material type; option C uses two properties, violating the “one property” rule; option D ignores properties altogether.

mcqs.learning_point: Creating groups using more than one property
mcqs.question: If you first separate objects into magnetic and non‑magnetic groups and then each of those groups into heavy and light sub‑groups, what is the maximum number of distinct groups you can obtain?
mcqs.explanation: Two categories from the first property (magnetic, non‑magnetic) each split into two categories (heavy, light). 2 × 2 = 4 distinct groups. The other numbers do not reflect the product of the two binary classifications.
